module

public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.InfiniteSum.Order

@[expose] public section

variable {ι α : Type*} [PartialOrder α] [CommGroup α] [IsOrderedMonoid α] [UniformSpace α]
  [IsUniformGroup α] [CompleteSpace α] [OrderClosedTopology α]
  {f : ι → α} {s : Finset ι} {t : Set ι}

@[to_additive]
protected lemma Multipliable.prod_le_tprod_set (hst : ↑s ⊆ t) (hfst : ∀ i ∉ s, i ∈ t → 1 ≤ f i)
    (hf : Multipliable f) : ∏ i ∈ s, f i ≤ ∏' i : t, f i := by
  rw [tprod_subtype, Finset.prod_congr rfl]
  refine (hf.mulIndicator t).prod_le_tprod _ (by simpa [Set.mulIndicator, apply_ite])
  rintro i hi
  simp [Set.mulIndicator, hst hi]

review.notes: Checked both declarations: Multipliable.prod_le_tprod_set and its generated additive counterpart Summable.sum_le_tsum_set. The file introduces no definitions. Both give the standard finite-subset comparison, requiring factors ≥ 1 or summands ≥ 0 only on t \ s. Global multipliability/summability and completeness guarantee convergence of the restricted family, so divergent-product/sum fallback values are unreachable. The only explicit caller is HasFejerGaps.hasFabryGaps in Analysis/HasGaps.lean, which uses precisely this meaning; neither declaration is directly referenced by a problem file. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled successfully with checks for empty indices and sets, equal subsets, singleton and trivial cases, signed finite examples, an infinite geometric example, and the caller's interval bound including N = 0. Both declarations have no sorryAx dependency. The reviewed file exactly matches the specified commit; no checkout files were edited.
